subject: Recap: observability & evals discovery — next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
To: Taylor Brooks <taylor@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: observability & evals discovery — next steps

Hi Taylor —

Thanks again for taking time today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the success criteria you shared, and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Lack of per-request tracing into model decisions (hard to tie hallucinations to a prompt or model version)
- No easy way to track quality regressions after model rollouts; tests live in spreadsheets and aren't automated
- Cost spikes from repeat inference on similar prompts; no prefix caching or targeted batching today

Current stack (what you told us):
- Inference: self-hosted GPU cluster running a mix of open LLMs via a homegrown API
- Observability: Grafana + application logs; no token-level tracing into model internals
- CI/Evals: Manual CSV-based prompt sets and post-hoc human review

Success criteria for a pilot/PoC:
- Visibility: per-request tracing hooks that include prompt, model version, and KV-cache fingerprinting
- Evals: automated golden-prompt runbook with pass/fail thresholds and regression alerts
- Dashboards: 3 dashboards — (1) Quality trend (passes/fails by prompt set), (2) Latency & cost per route, (3) Rollout health (errors, fallback rate)
- Guardrails: rollout policy that auto-fails to previous variant if regression threshold exceeded across golden prompts

Requested deliverables from Redwood (your list):
- Demo dashboards for Quality trend + Rollout health (sample data)
- Tracing hook spec (simple header + request XOR to link traces to crowdsourced logs)
- Starter golden prompt set (we attached our initial CSV: finlytics_eval_prompts_v1.csv)
- PoC plan with owners and timeline (2–3 week technical validation)

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses):
- Send back an annotated golden-prompt CSV with expected labels from FinLytics (Taylor) — due: Tue 6/16
- Redwood to provide a short PoC scope doc and access requirements (Ben) — due: Fri 6/12
- Setup a technical onboarding call to wire tracing headers and a read-only test endpoint (Jonas + FinLytics infra) — propose 6/17 or 6/18

Attachments: finlytics_eval_prompts_v1.csv (thanks for sharing), and I attached a lightweight diagram request for the PoC we discussed.

Appreciate the clarity — excited to help make your rollout safer and cheaper.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap: observability & evals discovery — next steps

Adding a few technical clarifications we should confirm on the PoC scope:

1) Tracing hooks
- We'll expose a lightweight header (X-Trace-Id / X-Model-Commit) that can be injected by FinLytics upstream. That will be sufficient to join application traces to inference requests in our tracing store.
- We'll provide a tiny reference middleware (Python/Node) to demonstrate header injection and retrieval.

2) Golden-prompt automation
- Redwood can run golden prompt sets automatically on every model rollout and emit a pass/fail per prompt; we can map that back to a Prometheus metric and Grafana dashboard.

3) Caching / cost controls
- Continuous prefix/KV caching is supported in our runtime; for PoC we'll suggest a conservative cache TTL and a route-level batching config so we don't change semantics but reduce unit cost.

4) Data concerns
- We will document retention windows for traces and evaluation results; by default PoC data retention = 30 days. If procurement needs HSM/KMS notes for keys we should bubble that into the security addendum.

PoC deliverable (high level):
- 2 weeks technical setup (headers, test endpoint) + 1 week run of golden prompts and data capture + 1 week analysis and dashboard handoff (total 4 weeks)

Ben — can you put together the short PoC scope doc (one pager) and share the access checklist? I'll drop a draft into the Drive link and tag it to the HubSpot record.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap: observability & evals discovery — next steps

Agree with Ben's plan. Proposed timeline and owners (short):
- 6/14: Ben publishes PoC scope doc to Drive (ben) — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c

- 6/25: Analyze results and deliver dashboards + handoff (Neha + Ben)

I'll also prepare the Grafana dashboard templates for: Quality Trend, Rollout Health, and Cost-by-Route.

If Taylor/procurement can confirm the security points (retention, keys) we can include that in the contract language.

-Jonas
